text:
oliver_finance: FYI - we got a question from Atlas Labs about an extra line on their Dedicated commit invoice (INV-2025-1055). They say this was unexpected and point to a vendor passthrough fee. Can billing/eng confirm?

mehran_billing: I pulled INV-2025-1055. Relevant lines: 
```
Dedicated Commit (monthly) - Apr 2025: $15,000
Third-party GPU passthrough surcharge - Apr 12: $3,600
Burst overage - Apr 12: $0 (covered by commit)
SLA credit: $0
```
Customer says passthrough wasn't in their SOW. We need to identify origin.

zara_cs: Atlas claims nothing changed in their settings. They escalated to account exec. Can Eng confirm if we forwarded traffic to a third-party provider that triggers a surcharge?

mike_devops: Checking infra routing. On Apr 12 during a scheduled capacity rebal there was an overflow placement to a partner GPU fleet (partner-nyc-a) for ~4m, due to one Dedicated pod hitting a memory allocation bug. The runtime normally prefers partner pools only when committed capacity is exhausted, but a bug in the placement policy allowed partner fallback when mem pressure > 0.

mehran_billing: That placement would explain the passthrough line. Do we have cost data? How was the $3,600 calculated?

mike_devops: Quick calc: partner hourly rate is $150/hr per GPU, two GPUs used for ~12h equivalent across all routed requests. Billing aggregator computed a prorated passthrough of $3,600. I can attach the placement logs and partner invoice excerpt.

oliver_finance: If the customer had reserved commit that should have covered their normal usage. Was this partner placement avoidable?

mike_devops: Avoidable - it's a bug. We patched the allocation policy so partner pools only qualify after commit exhaustion and for windows >15min. Also added a telemetry flag so billing can filter partner placements for outage credits.

zara_cs: Atlas wants either a credit or to be rebilled without the passthrough. They gave contract that includes "no passthrough without consent" clause.

mehran_billing: From billing perspective, we can issue a manual credit if ops confirms the placement was our error. Proposed credit = $3,600. Alternatively, we could absorb only 50% if Finance wants to split with partner, but partner invoice shows we were billed full. Need Finance sign-off.

oliver_finance: Let's absorb the full $3,600 as a one-off goodwill to preserve the relationship, but tag it as DED-PARTNER-MISPLACEMENT. We should start a negotiation with partner to recover the cost if possible. Also propose a pricing experiment: add an explicit passthrough consent checkbox on Dedicated onboarding to avoid surprises.

mehran_billing: Approved. I'll create adjustment ADJ-9421 for $3,600 credit and include log evidence and partner invoice. Billing-bot: please create BIL ticket and record reason code.

billing-bot: Ticket created: BIL-4499 - "Credit ADJ-9421 for INV-2025-1055 (DED-PARTNER-MISPLACEMENT)". Audit trail started.

mike_devops: I'll open partner recovery request referencing partner invoice PID-7783 and BIL-4499. We also pushed the allocation policy change and a short postmortem to infra-ops.

zara_cs: I'll notify Atlas with the credit confirmation and timeline. Please include the BIL ticket and what we changed to prevent recurrence.

oliver_finance: Good. Also add a note to Finance: trial the "passthrough consent" checkbox for new Dedicated customers next quarter and report back. Closing this thread; thanks. :white_check_mark:
